What if your AI coding agent is writing code before it fully understands what you want to build?

AI tools like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Google Antigravity can generate applications incredibly fast. But faster coding doesn't always mean better software.

What happens when your AI agent misunderstands requirements, misses important features, makes poor architectural decisions, or builds something completely different from your original idea?

This is where the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) comes in!

Introduced as an open-source plugin by Google engineers on October 22, 2026, EGM brings a structured, design-first approach to AI-assisted software development.

Instead of jumping directly into coding, EGM focuses on understanding requirements, preparing detailed specifications, reviewing potential problems, and approving the design before implementation.

What You'll Learn in This Video

•  What is the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM)?

•  Why AI coding agents can produce incorrect or incomplete applications

•  How Google engineers approach AI-assisted software design

•  Elephant vs Goldfish understanding their different responsibilities

•  How context-rich AI agents create detailed development plans

•  How fresh, independent AI reviewers identify missing requirements and design flaws

•  What is Spec-Driven Development (SDD)?

•  How EGM helps improve AI coding workflows

•  How to install and use the Elephant-Goldfish Model

•  How to integrate EGM with Google Antigravity, Claude Code, and OpenAI Codex

•  A practical walkthrough of the EGM workflow for building an application

 Elephant vs Goldfish How Does It Work?

Elephant The Planner

The Elephant maintains deep project context, understands your requirements, explores technical decisions, and prepares a structured software design specification.

Goldfish The Reviewer

The Goldfish starts with a fresh context and independently reviews the proposed design. It challenges assumptions, identifies missing details, and checks whether the specification is ready for implementation.

Human  The Decision Maker

You review the recommendations, resolve important trade offs, and approve the final design before asking your coding agent to implement it.

The workflow:

Idea → Brainstorm → Design Specification → Independent Review → Human Approval → AI Coding

The goal is simple: Plan better, review earlier, and build software with greater confidence.

Who Should Watch This Video?

This tutorial is useful for software developers, AI engineers, vibe coders, Claude Code users, Google Antigravity users, Codex users, startup founders, and anyone building real world applications with AI.

Whether you're building a 3D website, SaaS product, business application, or AI powered tool, understanding how to plan and validate your application before coding can make your development process more reliable.

AI can write code. But good software still needs good decisions.

If you're serious about building production quality AI applications, this is an important workflow to understand.

videos.title: 10 Habits PhDs Must Unlearn To Build a Startup | Startup School
videos.description:
Google, Anthropic, and Databricks were all started by founders with PhDs. But they’re the exceptions. Most academic founders fail, because the instincts that get you published are the ones that can get you killed in a startup. Francois Chaubard knows both sides. He’s a visiting partner at YC and a current PhD student, and before that he was a researcher in Fei-Fei Li’s lab and the founder and CEO of Focal. In this episode of Startup School, Francois breaks down the ten mindset shifts you have to make to go from researcher to formidable founder. He'll cover how to thrive without deadlines or grades, the difference between an interesting idea and an important one, and why being the first to an idea can actually be a disadvantage.

videos.description:
What if changing your life is simpler than you think?

In this conversation with Mel Robbins, GaryVee shares powerful lessons on letting go of other people’s opinions, overcoming regret, and focusing on what truly matters.

Life is too short to live for anyone else. Start living for yourself.
Thanks for watching!
 
Gary Vaynerchuk is a serial entrepreneur and serves as the Chairman of VaynerX, the CEO of VaynerMedia, and the CEO and creator of VeeFriends. Gary is considered one of the leading global minds on what's next in culture, business, and the internet.

Known as "GaryVee," he is described as one of the most forward thinkers in business. He acutely recognizes trends and patterns early to help others understand how shifts in consumer attention impact the realities of the business world today. Gary's approach sits at the intersection of business and pop culture. He keenly understands how to bring brand relevance to the forefront. He is a prolific angel investor with early investments in companies like Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Venmo, Snapchat, Coinbase, and Uber.

Gary is an entrepreneur at heart – he builds businesses. Today, he helps Fortune 1000 brands leverage consumer attention through his full-service advertising agency, VaynerMedia, which has offices in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Miami, Toronto, Mexico City, London, Amsterdam, Sydney, Singapore, Tokyo, Bangkok, Delhi, and Kuala Lumpur. VaynerMedia is part of the VaynerX holding company, which also includes Gallery Media Group, The Sasha Group, VaynerSpeakers, and Tingley Lane Trading. Gary is the Co-Founder of VaynerSports, VCR Group, VaynerWatt, ArtOfficial, Resy, and Empathy Wines. He guided Resy and Empathy to successful exits -- which he later sold to American Express and Constellation Brands, respectively. He also owns a Major League Pickleball team called the 5s, is part owner of a Big3 basketball team, and is an investor in the revival of the SlamBall League.

In 2021, Gary created VeeFriends, an entertainment company that has become a rising powerhouse in modern entertainment and collectibles. Often described as Pokemon meets Sesame Street, the company leverages stories, games, events, collectibles, and technology to scale its character universe. Vaynerchuk also has negotiated partnerships with brand powerhouses such as Crocs, Fanatics, Macy’s/Toys “R” Us, Mattel’s UNO, Mattel’s Masters of the Universe, Moonbug Entertainment, Reebok, Squishmallows, Topps, and more.

Gary is also the founder and creator of VeeCon – a contemporary super conference that converges business and pop culture with innovation and technology. He is a six-time New York Times bestselling author, with titles including Crush It!, Jab, Jab, Jab, Right Hook, Twelve and a Half and Day Trading Attention. In addition to running multiple businesses, Gary documents his daily life as a CEO through his social media channels, which have more than 45 million followers and garner more than 300 million monthly impressions/views across all platforms. His podcast, "The GaryVee Audio Experience," ranks among the top podcasts globally.

Gary serves on the board of MikMak, Bojangles Restaurants, Global Citizen Forum, The Paley Center, and Pencils of Promise. He is also a longtime Well Member of charity: water.

Gary's life ambition is to buy the New York Jets.

videos.title: Leila Hormozi: Discipline Isn't a Trait, It's a System You Build
videos.description:
You can't think your way into confidence. Leila Hormozi tried. She wrote affirmations on her bathroom mirror and read them out loud. Nothing changed for her.

In this episode, Leila Hormozi and Jay Shetty talk about what finally worked. She moved across the country with $5,000 and took a sales job at a gym. Her first try at talking to a stranger ended with her hiding in a bathroom.

Leila explains why she says the market never puts a business under. She tells the story of a company that grew from $2 million to $90 million a year, then it fell to zero in six months.

She also shares why she tries to be bad at things on purpose. And she shows how she makes the things she wants easy to do and the things she doesn't want hard to get.

Learn why discipline isn't about willpower. And learn the one skill she says everyone in their 20s should build first.
